title: LLM 0.37.2 fixes two credential-routing paths to custom model endpoints
summary: Two published advisories describe OpenAI credentials reaching a configured third-party endpoint under specific settings. Version 0.37.2 changes those paths; teams should update affected environments and check provider routing with synthetic credentials.

sections.title: A small release changes an important boundary
sections.html:
LLM 0.37.2, released on November 11, 2026, fixes two ways a configured OpenAI API key could be sent to a custom API endpoint. The affected software is Simon Willison's LLM tool and library; these are not claims about every OpenAI-compatible client or the OpenAI API itself. Both published GitHub advisories rate their issue Moderate and identify 0.37.2 as patched. The release notes confirm the changed behavior.

The immediate audience is developers using LLM with third-party providers, proxies or self-hosted gateways, including scripts that select a provider through configuration. This research did not inspect any user's installation, credentials or network history. It therefore establishes the reported conditions and fix, not that a particular person was affected. A working response from a model would not itself reveal which credential had accompanied the request.

sections.title: A missing provider key could select the OpenAI environment key
sections.html:
GHSA-v9h7-jj4g-f862 covers versions from 0.6 through 0.37.1. A custom model specifies an api_base and an api_key_name, but no key is stored under that name. The vulnerable path falls back to OPENAI_API_KEY and sends that value to the custom endpoint. A misspelled alias or a fresh environment lacking the intended provider key can trigger the condition.

In 0.37.2 the release notes say this path reports a missing-key error instead. That failure is useful: it exposes incomplete configuration without silently substituting another provider's credential. The advisory also identifies a broader historical precedence problem in versions 0.6 through 0.7.1, fixed in 0.8. Do not assume that creating an alias was sufficient protection across every affected historical version.

For a regression test, the important assertion is the selected destination and credential source. Checking only that the model call returns text misses the boundary this patch repairs.

sections.title: An optional API-mode switch had a separate credential path
sections.html:
GHSA-r639-rr7r-x72w covers versions from 0.32a2 through 0.37.1. It concerns a custom api_base model with responses: true, run using -o chat_completions 1. When api_key_name was not set, the delegated Chat path could resolve the stored openai key or OPENAI_API_KEY and send it to that endpoint. The advisory says a correctly stored named provider key prevents this particular delegate leak.

The release notes also identify the corresponding llm openai endpoint invocation, affected from 0.32rc2 through 0.37.1, with Responses mode and the same option, run without --key. This is a conditional path, not a statement that all custom-endpoint requests disclosed a key. The reporter supplies synthetic reproduction tests and describes patch validation. Those are reporter-authored results; this research did not reproduce them.

The engineering lesson is that switching protocol modes can construct another client with different defaults. Tests should inspect the request made by that client, not only configuration on the original model object.

sections.title: Update the environment that actually runs the workload
sections.html:
The setup documentation gives upgrade routes for pip, pipx, uv and Homebrew. Use the route that owns the existing installation, then verify the version used by the actual script, notebook, scheduled job or CI environment. Updating an interactive terminal's tool does not establish that an isolated project environment or container uses the same version. Check dependency locks and rebuilt images where those are part of the deployment.

Next, review the endpoint configuration without displaying secret values. Inventory custom API bases, named-key aliases and any workflow using the protocol-mode option. Use a mock transport or an endpoint under your control with synthetic sentinel credentials to check missing-key and correctly configured cases. Never use a live credential to demonstrate the leak. The proposed acceptance result is explicit: an absent named provider key produces an error, and a custom provider request never receives an unrelated OpenAI credential.

If an affected configuration was used, assess exposure from its actual destinations and history. Rotate a credential when that assessment indicates it may have reached an unintended recipient. The published bug alone does not prove disclosure in a particular environment.

sections.title: Make provider routing part of ordinary application tests
sections.html:
In an education workshop, learners can build a small matrix using fake endpoints and synthetic credentials: provider alias present or absent, stored key or environment key, ordinary mode or the delegate option. The deliverable is an explanation of which request is permitted and which must fail. Keep this a local exercise so students learn configuration isolation without handling real account secrets.

For an application or website backend, retain a similar regression test next to provider-selection code. Feed the adapter a configured destination and harmless prompt, intercept the outgoing request, and assert that its authorization source belongs to that destination. Include missing configuration and mode changes. This is a proposed test design, not evidence that a particular application integrates LLM or is vulnerable.

A video or audio team using LLM for script drafting, transcript analysis or production automation should examine the same backend boundary. The patch does not improve media generation or editing quality; its relevance is protecting credentials when a workflow routes requests among providers. Review logs and example configuration before sharing a debugging recording so that an instructional demonstration does not expose a genuine secret.

sections.title: A documented fix with a narrow, useful adoption case
sections.html:
The release also addresses attachments, endpoint configuration parsing and an embedding-collection model-selection problem. Those changes are separate from the two credential advisories and should not be used as evidence of their security impact. The core recommendation here is limited: update affected LLM environments and test the precise routing conditions your workflow uses.

Primary release notes and both advisories were inspected. No installed package, exploit attempt or user's account was examined, and no independent patch validation was performed. Preserve that distinction when communicating the issue. The practical improvement is a more explicit boundary between a provider's destination and its credential, supported by regression tests that can fail before a real secret leaves the application.

The repository uses the Apache License 2.0, and the public advisories expose the affected conditions and proposed patch logic for inspection. Licensing and visible source make review possible; they do not certify every integration. Keep the local acceptance tests alongside the exact dependency version so a future upgrade can be checked against the same expected behavior.

useCases: Teach provider and credential isolation with synthetic local tests.
Add destination–credential regression checks to an app or website's model adapter.
Review provider routing in LLM-based script or transcript automation.
limitations: No user's environment was inspected; no claim that the user was affected.
Advisory and reporter tests are primary documentary evidence, not independently reproduced results.
These conditions concern LLM custom endpoint configuration and the specified modes; they do not describe all clients or all requests.

judgment: A targeted maintenance update for teams using LLM with custom providers. Check affected versions, update the runtime actually used and verify routing with synthetic credentials.
researchNote: Release notes, two public advisories and setup documentation inspected November 14, 2026 through public web extraction. No installation, network reproduction, private credential access or account audit performed. November 11 is the release/advisory date, not retrieval time.
